Derived (not a native CBS ArcGIS field): round(Foreign_pcnt / 100 * pop_approx). CBS's own live ArcGIS field list (both 'census_2022_setl_all_2021' and the statistical-area 'census_2022_stat_all_2021' layers, enumerated live 2026-08-23) has no foreign-resident COUNT field, only 'Foreign_pcnt' (a rate). 'Foreign_pcnt' is explicitly documented (see the foreignResidentRate feature above) as relative_to 'population' with resampling_weight 'population', i.e. the same pop_approx already wired as this schema's 'population' field -- so multiplying is a verified-consistent reconstruction, not a guess. Computed by pycensus.countries.israel.cbs.loader.load() after fetching (never fetched from ArcGIS directly, hence empty 'codes'). Live-verified 2026-08-23: Beersheba (SETL_CODE=9000) Foreign_pcnt=1.6, pop_approx=217580.00000000003 -> foreignBornPopulation=3481.
Share of households with a parking space. Verified live 2026-08-22: Beersheba (SETL_CODE=9000) Parking_pcnt=62.9.

CBS's own per-area dominant-religion classification code (live-verified 2026-08-25 against both the locality layer's 'Religion_Code' and the statistical-area layer's 'Religion_Stat_Code' fields, same code scheme in both: 1=Jewish, 2=Muslim, 3=Christian, 5=Druze, 6=Other religion). A single categorical code per area, not a population breakdown -- used internally by pycensus.countries.israel.cbs.loader.load() to derive the 5 real per-religion population columns below (jewishPopulation, muslimPopulation, ...), then dropped before returning (a raw 1-6 category code is meaningless to sum/average, unlike those derived counts). Not itself exposed as a column.

Derived (not a native CBS ArcGIS field): population of areas whose religionCode == 1 (Jewish), i.e. pop_approx where the area's dominant-religion classification is Jewish lowercase, else 0. CBS reports religion as a single per-area categorical classification (see the religionCode feature above), not a population breakdown -- this reconstructs a real, verified per-religion population count from that classification, analogous to foreignBornPopulation's derivation below. Computed by pycensus.countries.israel.cbs.loader.load() after fetching (never fetched from ArcGIS directly, hence empty 'codes').

CBS's own per-area 'degree of religiosity' classification code among the Jewish population (live-verified 2026-08-25 against both the locality and statistical-area layers, same field name and code scheme on both: 1=secular (חילוני), 2=traditional (מסורתי), 3=religious/very religious (דתי/דתי מאוד), 4=Haredi/ultra-Orthodox (חרדי), 6=other (אחר). A single categorical code per area (real variation confirmed for Beersheba's statistical areas: 51 secular / 15 traditional / 1 religious / 16 unclassified out of 83), not a population breakdown -- used internally by pycensus.countries.israel.cbs.loader.load() to derive the 5 real per-category population columns below, then dropped before returning (a raw 1-6 category code is meaningless to sum/average). Not itself exposed as a column.

Derived (not a native CBS ArcGIS field): population of areas whose religiosityCode == 1, i.e. pop_approx where the area's dominant religious-observance classification matches that code, else 0. Named distinctly from the global-schema canonical 'religiousPopulation' feature (a different concept -- 'has any religion affiliation' vs. this field's 'degree of observance among the Jewish population') to avoid a semantic collision on canonical-name matching.
